text:
lina: Heads-up — hit a nasty generator+context race in the Go sample app when the auth token refresh runs while we're mid-stream. Repro attached (small, flaky).

ashley: Ugh, can you paste the repro snippet + logs?

lina: Yep — minimal snippet below. Note I'm using Background in the sample which may be part of the problem:

```go
// sample.go (bad)
ctx := context.Background()
g := client.NewGenerator(ctx, client.Opts{Model: "x"}) // <-- background used here
defer g.Close()
it := g.Stream("hello")
for it.Next() {
    fmt.Println(it.Value().Text)
    // simulate client cancel via external signal
}
if err := it.Err(); err != nil {
    log.Printf("stream err: %v", err)
}
```

logs: 
```
panic: send on closed channel
goroutine 123 [running]:
github.com/redwood/inference/gen.(*streamer).push(0xc000...)
...
```

lina: Repro steps: run sample, trigger token refresh (short TTL) while iterating, then cancel handler ctx; sometimes the iterator panics or returns duplicate Close errors.

sam: Two quick smells: 1) Using Background loses request-scoped cancellation; 2) token refresh path can race with stream teardown if refresh closes internal transport or replaces token source concurrently. We should ensure token refresh is singleflight or otherwise serialized for a connection.

sam: Quick suggestion — bind the generator lifecycle to the request context and the iterator, and keep token refresh isolated. e.g.:

```go
// handler 
func Handler(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {
    g := client.NewGenerator(req.Context(), client.Opts{Model: "x"})
    it := g.Stream("hi")
    defer it.Close() // tie cleanup to the iterator not the client global
    for it.Next() {
        io.WriteString(w, it.Value().Text)
    }
}
```

sam: Also wrap token refresh in a singleflight so only one goroutine executes the refresh and others wait — avoids mid-stream transport swaps.

ashley: Do we want to change the Go SDK surface? E.g., make Stream return an iterator type with Close() error and remove client-level Close() for basic streams. That would make ownership clearer.

mike: I like that. Fewer surprises for users. We should add a small integration test that forces concurrent refresh + cancel and assert no panics and deterministic error returns.

lina: I'll prepare a tiny PR in sample-app replacing Background with req.Context and add the integration test. Question: is a minor API change (iterator Close ownership) acceptable, or do we need to sync with parity team first?

ashley: Sync with SDK-parity and eng-ml to be safe. If it's a non-breaking addition (return new iterator type but keep old API as shim) we can land behind a flag. :+1:

infra-bot: ticket created: INF-3124 — "go sdk: generator stream lifecycle races with auth refresh" (assigned to lina)

sam: Also add a short note to the DX docs about "avoid context.Background for request-bound generators" and an example of token-refresh singleflight. People keep copying the sample.

lina: Will do. I'll open the PR and link INF-3124, add the test, and prototype the iterator-change as a follow-up. Thanks for the quick triage. :heart:

ashley: Thanks — ping me when PR is ready, will route to parity for review.

mike: Quick nit — add a repro script that toggles TTL to make the flake deterministic (low TTL + forced refresh). That helped me repro locally.

lina: Good call, will include script.

ashley: Awesome. Keeping this small and documented should help onboarding friction a lot.
